title: Fat Bear Week: Vote for the Chubbiest Bear in Alaska!
summary:
Imagine a bear so round and chubby that people all over the world vote for it. That's Fat Bear Week! It happens every year at Katmai National Park in Alaska, where about 2,200 brown bears live.

The contest started in 2014. A park ranger named Mike Fitz saw two photos of the same bear — one from June, one from September. The bear had gotten SO much fatter. That's because bears need lots of fat to survive the long, cold winter. Fitz turned the idea into a fun online contest.

Here's how it works: Each day, fans vote online for one of two bears in a head-to-head matchup. The bear with more votes moves on. The other is out. This keeps going until only two bears are left. The final vote is on September 29, 2026.

This year, 16 bears and bear families are competing. Bear 32, called Chunk, is back to defend his title after recovering from a broken jaw. Bear 164, or Bucky, is famous for snatching salmon out of the air. Bear 132 is raising three cubs. And Bear 806 is caring for her own cub plus an adopted one named Biggie.

In 2025, more than 1.7 million votes came in from over 100 countries. Not bad for a bunch of chubby bears!
why_it_matters: It shows kids that learning about animals can be fun, and that even a silly online contest can help people care about protecting nature.

background_read: Katmai National Park (a huge protected wild area in Alaska, the far northwest state of the U.S.) is famous for its brown bears, which gather at a waterfall called Brooks Falls to catch salmon.
Alaska has long, freezing winters, so bears eat as much as they can in summer and then sleep through the cold months — this is called hibernation.
Fat Bear Week started as a fun way to teach people about bears and about keeping rivers and wild places healthy.
Article_Structure: WHO: Park rangers at Katmai National Park, fans in over 100 countries, and 16 bears and bear families — including Chunk, Bucky, Bear 132, and Bear 806.
WHAT: An online contest where people vote in head-to-head matchups, round after round, until one chubby bear wins.
WHERE: Katmai National Park in Alaska, home to about 2,200 brown bears; the voting happens online.
WHY: Bears need a lot of fat to survive the long, cold winter, and the contest gets people around the world excited about wildlife.

perspectives.description: They like the contest because it teaches millions of people how bears grow fat for winter and why a healthy river full of salmon matters.
They worry that joking about how fat an animal is makes body size funny, or that people care more about voting than about the real dangers bears face.
They see it as a yearly tradition that brings free attention to the park — and gives scientists a way to tell the story of each individual bear.
